title: Kill
wikitext:
'''Kill''' is a keyword that refers to causing the death of an enemy. '''Killing blow''' is a keyword that refers to [[hit]]s that kill. __TOC__ ==Mechanics== Kills on a specific character can be checked using the /kills command. Kills are tracked up to approximately 16 million, after which it states, "You have killed an uncountable number of monsters."https://www.reddit.com/r/pathofexile/comments/1alspi1/what_happens_if_you_kill_too_many_monsters/ ===Awarding credit for kills=== When a target is killed, the kill is credited to the entity that dealt the killing blow, or if the target died to [[damage over time]], to the entity that inflicted the target's oldest damaging debuff.https://www.reddit.com/r/pathofexile/comments/46622m/mechanics_question_essence_drain_contagion/d02s2qk/?context=1 Kills by [[minion]]s or [[proxies]] are normally credited to the minion or proxy, and will not trigger the player's on-kill effects, though exceptions exist: * The player is always credited for the purpose of [[experience]], [[drop rate|loot]], on-kill [[flask charge]]s, [[rampage]], [[Vaal skill]] souls, and the intentional exceptions of {{il|Headhunter}} and {{il|Inspired Learning}}. * Kills by [[damage over time]] from minions or proxies are usually credited to the owner of the minion or proxy. This workaround exists to prevent attributing kills to entities that may have been deleted or replaced, and applies even if the minion/proxy still exists. This is a limitation of the game and not an intended game mechanic. ** This workaround primarily affects damage over time with a [[duration]]. ** Effects that necessarily have a living source such as {{il|Infernal Legion Support}} or {{il|Searing Bond}} do not have the kill credit workaround, as they do not need it. ** Other damage over time effects may not have the workaround due to skill-specific mechanics (e.g. {{il|Siphoning Trap}}) or bugs (e.g. {{il|The Retch}}). Kill credit may be obtained through {{il|Gravebind}}. This does not interact with killing blows, which are still dealt by the entity that actually dealt the hit. ===Corpses=== {{Main|Corpse}} Most enemies leave corpses on death. [[Totem]]s, [[shatter]]ed enemies, and enemies that are destroyed (e.g. {{il|Pyre}}, {{il|Kitava's Feast}}) don't leave corpses. Corpses can be utilized in several ways, for example: * raised (e.g. {{il|Raise Spectre}}, [[Necromancer (monster type)|Necromancer]] monsters) * created (e.g. {{il|Desecrate}}, {{il|Unearth}}) * [[explode]]d (e.g. {{il|Detonate Dead}}, {{il|Volatile Dead}}, {{il|Cremation}}, {{il|Bodyswap}}, [[strongbox]]es with the {{Ml|ChestExplodeCorpses}} prefix) * consumed (e.g. [[Offering]], {{il|Devouring Totem}}, {{il|Dominating Blow}}, {{il|Void Sphere}}, {{sl|Feast of Flesh}} (from {{il|The Devouring Diadem}}), etc.) Corpses can be targeted by holding the {{key press|A}} key by default, but only if the player has a skill that can target corpses. {{See also|Corpse skill gems}} ===On/when kill effects=== Similarly to [[Hit#On/when hit effects|on-hit effects]], there are effects that trigger when creature has been killed: * gain temporary [[buff]]s (e.g. [[charge]]s) * [[Gain on kill|gain life, mana or energy shield]] * skill-specific effects (e.g. {{il|Infernal Blow}}'s explosion) ==List of on kill effects== ===Unique items=== ====Gain on kill==== {{main|Gain on kill}} {{Drop enabled unique item table |tables=item_stats |join=items._pageID=item_stats._pageID |where= (item_stats.id LIKE "%gain%on_kill%" OR item_stats.id LIKE "%gain%on_enemy_death%" OR item_stats.id LIKE "%gain%on_killing%" OR item_stats.id LIKE "%recover%on_kill%") AND (item_stats.id LIKE "%life%" OR item_stats.id LIKE "%mana%" OR item_stats.id LIKE "%energy%shield%") |level=1 |stat_column1_header=Life gained
